title: Dodge Timeline editor is rendered by no route or nav entry
body:
## Summary
DodgeTimelineEditor, the context's entry point, has zero importers anywhere in src/, so the whole 16-file dodge tool is unreachable in the app.

## Description
`src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_combat/dodge-timeline/index.tsx:27` exports DodgeTimelineEditor; `git grep DodgeTimelineEditor` finds only the definition, a harness type comment (`src/lib/harness/types.ts:62`) and an unused props interface (`src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_combat/_shared/dodge-types.ts:51`). `src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_combat/CombatNav.tsx` and `src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_combat/index.tsx` contain no 'dodge'. The context map describes it as a tool combat designers use. Fixed means either a combat nav entry that renders it, or a decision to retire the context.

## Flow
- open the Combat module -> no tab or subtab renders the dodge timeline
- git grep DodgeTimelineEditor -> 1 definition, 0 JSX consumers
- decide: wire into CombatNav (product direction) or retire the 16 files

## Expected impact
Combat designers gain (or the repo sheds) a whole tool; wiring it adds a tab to a nav owned by another context.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the dodge tooling becomes reachable (or is retired)
Before: 0 importers of DodgeTimelineEditor; 0 nav entries
After: 1 nav entry rendering it, or 0 files
Method: probe - git grep over src/ for the export and the folder path; whether to wire it is a product call
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
evidence:
git grep -n DodgeTimelineEditor -- src -> dodge-timeline/index.tsx:27 (definition), src/lib/harness/types.ts:62 (comment), _shared/dodge-types.ts:51 (unused interface)
grep -n dodge sub_combat/CombatNav.tsx sub_combat/index.tsx -> no hits
instrument: operator decision: wire into CombatNav or retire

title: Single-source the hit-dodged predicate (5 inline copies)
body:
## Summary
Whether a hit lands inside the i-frame window is re-derived inline at 5 sites, one of them from params instead of phases.

## Description
`src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_combat/dodge-timeline/useDodgeTimelineState.ts:24` (haptic: params.iFrameStart .. +iFrameDuration), `src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_combat/dodge-timeline/useDodgeTimelineState.ts:46` (stats), `src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_combat/dodge-timeline/TimelineBarMarkers.tsx:22`, `src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_combat/dodge-timeline/HitMarkerEditor.tsx:50` and `src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_combat/dodge-timeline/HitMarkerEditor.tsx:95` (phases.invuln). They agree today only because computePhases maps the params 1:1; any change to the window rule (inclusive end, grace frames, trigger grades) must be made five times. Fix: export isHitDodged(phases, t) from dodge-timeline/types.ts and route all five through it.

## Flow
- add isHitDodged(phases, t) in dodge-timeline/types.ts with boundary tests
- replace the 5 inline expressions
- comment-stripped source guard: the inline comparison appears only in the helper

## Expected impact
Marker dots, haptics, editor rows and counts give identical DODGED/HIT verdicts by construction; nothing user-visible changes today.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one rule, one implementation
Before: 5 inline copies of the predicate, 1 of them reading params
After: 1 helper, 0 inline copies
Method: simulation - counted sites by grep; the guard test was not built this round (budget)
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
useDodgeTimelineState.ts:24 hit.time >= params.iFrameStart && hit.time < params.iFrameStart + params.iFrameDuration
useDodgeTimelineState.ts:46 h.time >= phases.invuln.start && h.time < phases.invuln.end
TimelineBarMarkers.tsx:22, HitMarkerEditor.tsx:50, HitMarkerEditor.tsx:95 same expression
instrument: source-scan guard counting inline copies (5 -> 0) plus a boundary unit test for isHitDodged

title: Hit marker time accepts values past the timeline end
body:
## Summary
The hit-time number input does not clamp, so a hit typed at 5s renders its dot outside the bar and is silently counted as a HIT.

## Description
`src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_combat/dodge-timeline/HitMarkerEditor.tsx:65` passes `parseFloat(value) || 0` straight to onUpdate; the max attribute is not enforced on typed input and negatives pass too. `src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_combat/dodge-timeline/TimelineBarMarkers.tsx:21` then positions it at left > 100% inside an overflow-hidden bar, so it vanishes. ParameterEditor clamps its number inputs (`src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_combat/dodge-timeline/ParameterEditor.tsx:69`); the hit editor is the unclamped twin. Fix: clamp time to [0, phases.totalTimeline] in index.tsx updateHitMarker.

## Flow
- open Incoming Hit Timing, type 5 in a hit's time
- the dot disappears from the bar (left 384%), the row reads HIT
- clamp in updateHitMarker for field 'time'

## Expected impact
Designers cannot create invisible hit markers; a time typed past the end pins to the end.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - hit times stay on the timeline
Before: typed 5 / -1 accepted verbatim (0 clamps on this input vs 1 on the ParameterEditor twin)
After: clamped to [0, 1.3] on defaults
Method: simulation - read the handler and the positioning math; the component test was not written this round
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
HitMarkerEditor.tsx:65 onChange={(e) => onUpdate(hit.id, 'time', parseFloat(e.target.value) || 0)}
ParameterEditor.tsx:69 if (!isNaN(v)) onUpdate(f.key, Math.max(f.min, Math.min(f.max, v)));
instrument: component test: type 5 into a hit time, assert the stored time is <= phases.totalTimeline

title: Icon-only dodge buttons and the parameter inputs have no accessible name
body:
## Summary
Three icon-only buttons and every range/number input in the editor carry no aria-label, so screen readers announce 'button' / 'slider' with no meaning.

## Description
`grep aria-label` over dodge-timeline/ returns 0 across 10 buttons. Icon-only: `src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_combat/dodge-timeline/ChainControls.tsx:56` (Plus), `src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_combat/dodge-timeline/ChainControls.tsx:63` (Trash2), `src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_combat/dodge-timeline/HitMarkerEditor.tsx:78` (Trash2); HeaderToolbar ToggleBtn relies on title only (`src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_combat/dodge-timeline/HeaderToolbar.tsx:65`). ParameterEditor renders 8 opacity-0 range inputs and 8 number inputs next to a span, not a label (`src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_combat/dodge-timeline/ParameterEditor.tsx:56`). Fix: aria-label on the icon buttons, aria-label={f.label} on each param input and on the hit-row inputs.

## Flow
- tab into the chain controls -> focus lands on an unnamed button
- count controls with an empty accessible name by role query
- add labels; re-count

## Expected impact
Keyboard and screen-reader users can operate the editor; no visual change.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - every control has an accessible name
Before: 0 aria-labels; 3 icon-only buttons + 16 param inputs + 3 inputs per hit row unnamed
After: 0 unnamed controls
Method: simulation - counted by grep; the role-name test was not built this round
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
grep -c aria-label dodge-timeline/*.tsx -> 0; grep -c '<button' -> 10
ChainControls.tsx:56 <Plus className="w-3 h-3" /> (no text)
ParameterEditor.tsx:56 <input type="range" ... className="absolute inset-0 w-full opacity-0"> (no label)
instrument: render test counting controls with an empty accessible name (role query), before vs after

title: Dodge timeline scrub bars are mouse-only
body:
## Summary
TimelineBar and DodgeChainTimeline scrub only via mousedown/mousemove; there is no keyboard or touch path to move the playhead.

## Description
`src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_combat/dodge-timeline/TimelineBar.tsx:56` and `src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_combat/dodge-timeline/DodgeChainTimeline.tsx:49` attach onMouseDown from the shared useScrubBar (`src/hooks/useScrubBar.ts:28`), which listens to window mousemove only. The bars are plain divs: no role=slider, tabIndex, aria-valuenow or arrow keys; pointer (touch/pen) events are unused. Fix: role=slider + aria-value* + arrow keys stepping one frame (1/60 s) in this context; pointer events in the shared hook (outside this context).

## Flow
- tab through the editor -> no focus stop on the timeline
- touch-drag on a tablet -> nothing scrubs
- add slider semantics and arrow-key frame stepping

## Expected impact
Keyboard users can step a dodge frame by frame - the precise-tuning workflow the context exists for.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - playhead reachable without a mouse
Before: 0 keyboard paths to move the playhead (2 bars)
After: 2 bars focusable, arrow keys step 1 frame
Method: simulation - read both bars and the hook; the keyboard test was not built
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
TimelineBar.tsx:56 onMouseDown={onMouseDown} on a <div> with no role/tabIndex
src/hooks/useScrubBar.ts:21 window.addEventListener('mousemove', onMove)
instrument: render test: focus the bar, press ArrowRight, assert onScrub(1/60)

title: Chain mode or chain edits during playback are not reconciled with the running loop
body:
## Summary
play() captures chainMode, the chain and its end time when pressed; switching mode or rebuilding the chain while playing leaves the loop driving the old playhead to the old end.

## Description
`src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_combat/dodge-timeline/index.tsx:94` computes total and picks posRef once per Play. ChainControls' 2x/3x/4x buttons (`src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_combat/dodge-timeline/ChainControls.tsx:40`) call onSetChainMode + onBuildChain while isPlaying can be true; nothing pauses or retargets the loop, so the single-dodge playhead keeps advancing under a chain view, or a 4x chain plays only to the 2x end. Fix: pause in an effect keyed on chainMode/chain, or retarget from refs per frame.

## Flow
- press Play, then click 4x while playing
- the chain view appears; the loop still advances the single-dodge playhead
- pause on chainMode/chain change

## Expected impact
Designers comparing chains get a playhead that matches the chain on screen.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - one loop, one target, current end time
Before: loop target fixed at press time (chainMode/chain captured once)
After: loop paused or retargeted on change
Method: simulation - traced the play() closure and the ChainControls handlers; test not built
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
index.tsx:94-96 const total = chainMode ? getChainEndTime(chain) : phases.totalTimeline; const posRef = chainMode ? chainPlayheadRef : playheadRef;
ChainControls.tsx:40 onClick={() => { onSetChainMode(true); onBuildChain(n); }}
instrument: component test with the manual rAF clock from dodge-timeline-editor.test.tsx: Play, click 4x, tick, assert the single-dodge playhead stopped

title: Haptic flash durations are literals instead of UI_TIMEOUTS
body:
## Summary
The hit/dodge haptic flash clears after hard-coded 500/400 ms, against the repo rule that timing values come from UI_TIMEOUTS.

## Description
`src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_combat/dodge-timeline/useDodgeTimelineState.ts:27` setTimeout(..., dodged ? 500 : 400). CLAUDE.md: all timing values come from UI_TIMEOUTS in @/lib/constants.ts. The flash overlay in `src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_combat/dodge-timeline/TimelineBar.tsx:67` (0.45 / 0.3 s) is a second, independent pair of numbers for the same effect that can drift from the clear timer. Fix: two UI_TIMEOUTS keys used by both.

## Flow
- grep literal ms in dodge-timeline/
- add UI_TIMEOUTS keys (constants.ts is shared, outside this context)
- use them in the hook and the overlay transition

## Expected impact
No visible change; the clear timer and the flash animation stay in step when tuned.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - timing literals routed through UI_TIMEOUTS
Before: 2 literal timeouts + 2 independent animation durations for one effect
After: 0 literals; 1 source per duration
Method: probe - grep over the 16 files
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
useDodgeTimelineState.ts:27 timerRef.current = setTimeout(() => setEffect(null), dodged ? 500 : 400);
TimelineBar.tsx:67 transition={{ duration: isDodgeHaptic ? 0.45 : 0.3 }}
instrument: grep count of setTimeout literals in dodge-timeline/ (2 -> 0); touches shared src/lib/constants.ts (out-of-scope seam)

title: Stamina bar size 100 is hard-coded in two places
body:
## Summary
Max stamina is a literal 100 in the chain timeline and in the frame-data efficiency metric, with no shared constant.

## Description
`src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_combat/dodge-timeline/DodgeChainTimeline.tsx:30` const maxStamina = 100; and `src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_combat/dodge-timeline/FrameDataTable.tsx:34` Math.floor(100 / params.staminaCost). Both encode one rule (a full bar = 100); the 'Stamina Efficiency' rating and the chain's depletion curve disagree the moment either changes. Fix: one MAX_STAMINA export in dodge-timeline/types.ts consumed by both.

## Flow
- grep the literal in dodge-timeline/
- extract MAX_STAMINA
- use it in both files

## Expected impact
No visible change today; a stamina tune moves both readouts together.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one stamina constant
Before: 2 literal copies
After: 1 constant, 2 consumers
Method: probe - grep
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
DodgeChainTimeline.tsx:30 const maxStamina = 100;
FrameDataTable.tsx:34 ? Math.floor(100 / params.staminaCost) : Infinity;
instrument: grep count of the literal (2 -> 0) plus a FrameDataTable dodgesPerBar test

title: HapticEffect and DodgeTimelineEditorProps duplicated or unused in _shared
body:
## Summary
HapticEffect is declared in dodge-timeline/types.ts and again in _shared/dodge-types.ts; DodgeTimelineEditorProps in _shared has no consumer.

## Description
`src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_combat/dodge-timeline/types.ts:7` and `src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_combat/_shared/dodge-types.ts:49` define the same union; every importer uses the local one (`src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_combat/dodge-timeline/TimelineBar.tsx:10`, `src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_combat/dodge-timeline/index.tsx:11`). `src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_combat/_shared/dodge-types.ts:51` DodgeTimelineEditorProps: 0 importers (index.tsx types its prop inline). _shared belongs to combat-metrics, so the deletion is outside this round's paths.

## Flow
- git grep HapticEffect / DodgeTimelineEditorProps
- delete the _shared copies (combat-metrics owner)
- typecheck

## Expected impact
None for users; one fewer drift point.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - dead duplicate types removed
Before: 2 HapticEffect declarations; 1 unused props interface
After: 1 declaration; 0 unused
Method: probe - git grep for consumers
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
_shared/dodge-types.ts:49 export type HapticEffect (0 importers)
_shared/dodge-types.ts:51 export interface DodgeTimelineEditorProps (0 importers)
instrument: typecheck green after deletion; git grep consumer count 0 (out-of-scope: _shared is combat-metrics)

title: Frame-data '@60fps' column restates Seconds with a literal 60
body:
## Summary
FrameDataTable declares FPS = 60 but the '@60fps' column divides by a literal 60 and the footnote and legend hard-code '60 FPS', so the constant does not govern the table.

## Description
`src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_combat/dodge-timeline/FrameDataTable.tsx:18` const FPS = 60; `src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_combat/dodge-timeline/FrameDataTable.tsx:114` (row.frames / 60).toFixed(3); the footnote (`src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_combat/dodge-timeline/FrameDataTable.tsx:71`) and `src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_combat/dodge-timeline/PhaseLegend.tsx:40` '@60 FPS' are literals. The column is the frame-quantized seconds, useful only if labelled so. Fix: use FPS everywhere and label the column 'Quantized'.

## Flow
- grep 60 in FrameDataTable/PhaseLegend
- route through FPS
- rename the header

## Expected impact
Changing the target frame rate (30/120 fps) becomes one edit; readers see what the 4th column means.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the FPS constant governs all frame math
Before: 1 of 4 sites uses FPS
After: 4 of 4
Method: probe - grep
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: FrameDataTable render test with FPS exported and patched, asserting the quantized column follows it
